questions.q: An IoT sensor fleet sends readings every second, needing continuous ingestion routed to a KQL database. What is the correct ingestion path?
options: A manual file upload to a Lakehouse
An Event Hub/IoT Hub source feeding an Eventstream, routed into an Eventhouse/KQL database
A Data Factory pipeline scheduled to run every minute
questions.explain: Pipelines and Dataflows are batch-oriented; the scenario's word 'continuously' points directly to an Eventstream (Fabric Lesson 19).

questions.q: Which KQL operators filter rows and then select specific columns, respectively?
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 23: where filters rows, project selects/renames columns — in that order for a filter-then-select query.

questions.q: What KQL pattern computes the average of a metric grouped into five-minute intervals?
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 24's summarize-with-bin pattern is KQL's time-bucketed aggregation — the same idea as a tumbling window, in query syntax.

questions.q: A scenario describes combining rows from two KQL tables based on a matching key column. Which KQL capability does this describe?
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 25 covers KQL joins for combining data across tables on a matching key.

questions.q: What is the role of an Eventhouse in a Fabric real-time solution?
options: It replaces the need for a Lakehouse entirely
It is a synonym for a Fabric capacity
It hosts the KQL database that Eventstreams route data into for near-real-time querying
It is a batch-only orchestration tool
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 21: Eventhouse and KQL Database is the destination that streaming Eventstream data lands in for querying.

questions.q: A KQL query needs to compute a moving statistic over time, like a rolling count of events per hour. Which category of KQL functions handles this?
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 26 covers KQL's time series functions for exactly this kind of rolling, time-based computation.

questions.q: Why would a scenario describing 'ingesting historical CSV files into a KQL database for backfill' point to a different mechanism than the live Eventstream path?
options: Because ingesting data into a KQL database can also happen through direct/batch ingestion (Fabric Lesson 27), not only through a live Eventstream
Because CSV files cannot be loaded into any Fabric item
Because Eventstreams are the only possible ingestion path into any KQL database
Because KQL databases can never receive batch or historical data
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 27 covers ingesting data into a KQL database directly, separate from the continuous Eventstream path.
